contexts.text: As fruits are filled with bitter juice, before they can receive sweet juice...
Like what is immature in fruits, by which the juice is introduced... At last the fruits ripen by the fibres of genuine juice.
These things... are represented in the juices of meats, which are immediately imbibed by the veins...
All the fibres of the fruit... nurse the germ by the percolating juice... But when it has been formed, the fibres... carry the juice away from the seed.
Embryos are nourished through the liver; for all the nutritious juice is brought thither... This juice corresponds to the good of innocence.
They colour the web with the juices of herbs.
A tree... extracts from the ground... a grosser juice for the trunk, branches, and leaves; a purer one for the fleshy parts of the fruit; and the purest for the seeds. AE 1084:4.

A tree which is evil from its seed and root introduces its evil juices into the stem of a tree which is grafted upon it; and the evil juices... are turned into good juices, and produce useful fruits. So with man...
When the earth first opens a seed... from the root, which is a kind of heart, it emits and transmits sap, like blood, and so makes as it were a body.
The flowers which precede the fruit are means for decanting the sap, which is its blood, and of separating its grosser from its purer parts...
Religion... passes up through the civil things of the world, as the pure sap passes through a tree to its very top...

What produces the universal tree, and forms it? It is nothing else than the sap, which is drawn up from the soil through the root, and which so unfolds itself that after passing through a gyre in nature, it again concentrates itself, first into fruits, then into seeds, and finally into the interior seminal essences... It is the same in the human mind; for the Knowledges of good and evil are for the sake of ends which are uses...

The sap in a tree is nothing but the interior and inmost essence in the seed, which... produces a root, through which a like sap is continually drawn up, which in the pores themselves is formed after the likeness of the first...
For as the sap is the life of a tree, so are the loves themselves the life of a man...
Let us inquire, further, what produces this sap, and excites it into its motion, so that the tree... comes forth from it...

As, then, it is heat which excites the sap of a tree into its motion... from this it may be evident that inmostly in the sap there is that which is excited; namely, that which corresponds to the heat itself, and is called its ray...
If they see any juice expressed (from the fibres) they will then believe.
Its taste was as the juice of oil ()... Its juice, from which was its taste, = its internal delight.
From the food... the fibres of the nerves draw forth their juice...
